findings.claim: The newly added `relaxedCookieNameRegEx` is not wired into any code in this hunk; if `parse()` still tests names with `validCookieNameRegEx`, the fix is a no-op and the constant is dead code (which also trips `noUnusedLocals`/lint in many TS setups).
findings.rationale: The diff only introduces the constant and comments. I cannot see the parse path in this hunk, so I'm not certain, but the change is only meaningful if the consuming code was updated in the same commit — worth verifying that `parse()`/`parseSigned()` actually switched to the relaxed regex.

findings.claim: Character class `[!#-:<>-[\]-~]` relies on an unescaped `[` as a range endpoint (`>-[`), which is legal under the default/`u` semantics but is a syntax error if the `v` flag is ever added, and is easy to misparse by humans and tooling.
findings.rationale: Verified the intended set matches the comment (33-126 minus 34, 59, 61, 92), so behavior today is correct; the concern is fragility/readability of the escaping, not current output. Escaping as `>-\[` would be safer. Confidence: high on the escaping fact, low on it causing a bug today.

findings.claim: Parsing and serialization now use different name grammars, so a cookie read from the request (e.g. `paraglide:lang`) can no longer be re-emitted through `setCookie`/`serialize` without throwing — a behavior change for middleware that copies or refreshes incoming cookies.
findings.rationale: This asymmetry is deliberate per the added comments, but callers that round-trip parsed names into `setCookie` will start hitting the strict-regex validation error for names that previously were simply dropped at parse time. Worth confirming the error is thrown (not silently swallowed) and documented. Medium confidence, since the serialize path is outside this hunk.
